newsitem.title: USA: IMF expects Venezuela to return to positive growth.
newsitem.headline: IMF expects Venezuela to return to positive growth.

text.p: Venezuela should return to positive economic growth in 1997 as its stabilization program takes root, IMF chief economist Michael Mussa said Wednesday.

"We anticipate, that with the implementation of the stabilization program now in effect, and with the gains in oil prices which should be helpful in Venezuela's case ... stabilization will be successful and Venezuela will return to positive growth," Mussa said at a news conference.

In its World Economic Outlook report released ahead of next week's joint meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, the IMF's staff said it expected Venezuela's GDP to contract by about 1.1 percent this year.

After trying unsuccessfully for several years to bring down inflation through price and exchange controls, Venezuela this year scrapped those measures and adopted a free market-oriented program supported by the IMF.
The IMF's report noted that Venezuela's inflation had accelerated to 7.5 percent a month during the first quarter of 1996 but expected it to abate substantially during the rest of the year.
